source_document.body:
The latest FreightWaves Freight Distress Report points to continued workforce reductions across trucking, third-party logistics, truck manufacturing, packaging and consumer goods production as the U.S. enters the holiday season .
Nine companies have announced workforce reductions affecting up to 7,656 workers, including Procter & Gamble’s long-term plan to eliminate as many as 7,000 manufacturing and logistics jobs. The remaining eight companies account for 656 job cuts tied to facility closures and contract losses.
The latest round of layoffs comes during what is traditionally one of the busiest periods of the year for retailers, trucking companies and distribution networks.
Procter & Gamble targets up to 7,000 supply chain jobs
Consumer goods giant Procter & Gamble Co. (NYSE: PG ) plans to reduce its manufacturing and logistics workforce by 20% to 30%, potentially eliminating as many as 7,000 positions by the end of the decade.
The reductions are part of a broader productivity initiative aimed at generating up to $10 billion in cumulative savings from fiscal 2027 through fiscal 2030.
The initiative includes an increased emphasis on automation, reflecting a broader shift among manufacturers toward technology-driven supply chain operations.
The planned reductions represent a longer-term restructuring rather than an immediate mass layoff.
Walgreens contract loss costs 66 truck drivers their jobs
CPC Special Logistics East LLC, a trucking contractor for Walgreens, expects to permanently lay off 69 employees in Connecticut after the retailer decided not to renew its contract.
In a Nov. 23 notice filed with the Connecticut Department of Labor, CPC said operations at Walgreens’ distribution center at 80 International Drive in Windsor and associated driver locations are expected to end around Jan. 30.
The affected employees include 66 commercial truck drivers, a regional manager, a safety manager and an administrative assistant.
The notice was issued three days before Thanksgiving.
Saddle Creek, GEODIS shutter logistics facilities
Third-party logistics provider Saddle Creek Corp. announced Nov. 19 that it will permanently close its facility in Groveport, Ohio, eliminating 150 jobs.
The layoffs are scheduled to begin Jan. 15.
Global logistics provider GEODIS also scheduled the permanent closure of an operation in Reno, Nevada, affecting 99 employees.
GEODIS filed its WARN notice Sept. 23, with the closure effective Nov. 22, just four days before Thanksgiving.
Morgan Truck Body closing Ohio manufacturing plant
Morgan Truck Body LLC is permanently closing its manufacturing plant in Orrville, Ohio, eliminating 73 jobs.
The company cited “unforeseeable business circumstances” in a WARN notice dated Nov. 18.
Morgan Truck Body manufactures commercial truck bodies used in freight transportation, distribution and last-mile delivery operations.
Packaging manufacturers eliminate nearly 100 jobs
Two packaging manufacturers are shuttering facilities in Pennsylvania and Missouri, eliminating a combined 96 positions.
J.L. Clark, a manufacturer of metal and plastic packaging products, plans to permanently close its facility in Lancaster, Pennsylvania, affecting 34 employees. The closure and layoffs are expected to be finalized in 2027.
Gateway Packaging Co. announced in a Nov. 20 notice that it will close its facility at 5910 Winner Road in Kansas City, Missouri.
The closure will leave 62 employees without jobs by Dec. 30, between Christmas and New Year’s Day.
Pepsi, Niagara Bottling closing production facilities
Workforce reductions are also affecting the beverage manufacturing sector.
Pepsi Bottling Group plans to permanently close its facility at 2708 Federal Road in Knoxville, Tennessee, eliminating 112 jobs effective Jan. 1.
The company notified the Tennessee Department of Labor and Workforce Development of the closure Oct. 19.
Niagara Bottling is also closing its water bottling plant in Ocala, Florida, affecting 57 employees. The layoffs are expected to be completed by the end of 2026.
Freight Distress Report: November 25, 2026

Source: WARN notices and company announcements compiled in the Nov. 25 Freight Distress Report.
Why it matters: Workforce reductions and distribution center closures ahead of the holidays highlight ongoing cost pressures and structural changes across the freight economy.
